title: Impact of Upwind Pollution on Infant Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The chosen method for this analysis is Instrumental Variables (IV) Regression. We use wind direction, denoted by the indicator variable `z` for upwind pollution source, as the instrument. The key assumptions for the validity of this instrument are:
- Relevance: Wind direction affects pollution exposure (`x`).
- Exogeneity: Wind direction does not directly affect infant mortality (`y`) other than through its impact on pollution exposure.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(AER)

# Load the dataset
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s75_data.csv"
data <- read.csv(data_path)

# Define the instrument
instrument <- data$z

# Run the IV regression: y ~ x | z + controls
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)

# Print the summary result
summary_iv <- summary(iv_model)
print(summary_iv)

# Extract and print the main coefficient (impact of pollution on infant mortality)
coef_estimate <- coef(summary_iv)["x", "Estimate"]
coef_pvalue <- coef(summary_iv)["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("IV Coefficient Estimate for Pollution on Infant Mortality: ", coef_estimate, "\n")
cat("p-value: ", coef_pvalue, "\n")

# Basic robustness checks: Run OLS for comparison
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
summary_ols <- summary(ols_model)
print(summary_ols)

# Check instrument relevance through first-stage regression
first_stage_model <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
summary_first_stage <- summary(first_stage_model)
print(summary_first_stage)

# Extract and print F-statistic for instrument relevance
f_statistic <- summary_first_stage$fstatistic
cat("First-stage F-statistic: ", f_statistic, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect the coefficient for pollution exposure (`x`) to be positive, indicating that higher levels of pollution are associated with increased infant mortality rates. The magnitude of this effect will depend on the strength of the instrument and the elasticity of infant mortality in response to pollution. Typically, substantial pollution changes can lead to notable increases in mortality risk, possibly in the range of 0.1 to 0.3 increase in mortality rate per unit increase in pollution exposure.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Wind direction is used as an instrument for pollution exposure.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Upwind pollution exposure is found to significantly increase infant mortality.
